# Results — Study 431 (Schaff Trend Cycle) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — the canonical STC
(fast 23, slow 50, cycle 10, smoothing 0.5) turned into a daily **long/flat** position (long on
a cross up through 25, flat on a cross down through 75), held between signals, entered with **one
execution lag** (signal at close *t* earns the *t+1* return), **net** of 1 bp one-way × NAV per
unit turnover. All Sharpe races are **excess-of-cash vs excess-of-cash**; closes are
**total-return adjusted** (yfinance `auto_adjust`). As-of **2026-05-31**.*

## The headline race — SPY long/flat, net (1 bp)

| Strategy | net Sharpe | CAGR | max drawdown | HAC *t* (vs 0) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **STC long/flat** | **0.29** | **2.95%** | −50.2% | **1.87** |
| Plain MACD crossover (12/26/9) | 0.42 | — | — | — |
| **Buy & hold** | **0.65** | **10.90%** | −55.2% | — |

- The STC rule's net Sharpe (**0.29**) is **below buy-and-hold (0.65)** — Δ = **−0.36** — and
  **below the plain MACD it claims to beat (0.42)**. It grows capital at **2.95%/yr** vs
  buy-and-hold's **10.90%/yr**, for a barely-better worst drawdown (−50% vs −55%).
- The rule's own edge against zero is **not significant**: HAC *t* = **1.87**, under the 2.0 bar.

## The significance test — block-permutation placebo

A 2,000-draw placebo that **block-shuffles the position** (21-day blocks, asset returns fixed),
asking whether the STC's *timing* beats randomly re-ordering its in-market days:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Observed mean net excess | +1.47 bps/day |
| Block-permutation *p* | **0.961** |

A shuffled position does as well or better **96%** of the time. The timing carries no
detectable information.

## Long/short variant — worse

| | net Sharpe | CAGR | max drawdown | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| STC long/short | **−0.26** | −6.42% | **−91.4%** | −1.75 |
| Plain MACD long/short | −0.16 | — | — | — |

Shorting on the down-cross loses money outright.

## Cost sweep (long/flat) — costs are not the killer

| one-way cost / flip | net Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | 0.31 | 1.96 |
| 1.0 bps | 0.29 | 1.87 |
| 2.0 bps | 0.28 | 1.78 |
| 5.0 bps | 0.24 | 1.51 |
| 10.0 bps | 0.17 | 1.07 |

Even at **zero cost** the STC Sharpe (0.31) never reaches buy-and-hold (0.65). The rule is on
the wrong side of the index's drift; costs (it flips ~17×/yr) only deepen the gap.

## Robustness panel (long/flat, 1 bp) — not SPY-specific

| Ticker | n | STC Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | MACD Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 8,390 | 0.29 | 0.65 | 0.42 | 1.87 |
| QQQ  | 6,848 | 0.20 | 0.52 | 0.21 | 1.07 |
| IWM  | 6,540 | 0.36 | 0.47 | 0.42 | 2.00 |
| EFA  | 6,225 | 0.26 | 0.41 | 0.19 | 1.45 |
| AAPL | 11,457 | 0.37 | 0.63 | 0.61 | 2.36 |
| MSFT | 10,131 | 0.43 | 0.84 | 0.57 | 2.70 |

STC **trails buy-and-hold on all six** names and **trails the plain MACD on 5 of 6**. AAPL/MSFT
clear *t* = 2 only because their *drift* is large — buy-and-hold beats STC there by the **widest**
margins, confirming the "edge" is leftover beta, not timing.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine works when there's a trend to find

A deterministic regime-trend panel (`data.synthetic_panel`): zero trend must not beat
buy-and-hold; a planted trend must light up.

| Planted trend | STC Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | Δ (STC − B&H) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.000 (null) | −0.35 | −0.16 | **−0.19** | −1.42 |
| 0.003 (real trend) | 0.82 | 0.72 | **+0.10** | **2.66** |

With no trend the rule loses to passive (no false positive); with a real trend planted it
**beats** buy-and-hold and clears *t* = 2. The harness can bank a genuine trend edge — the
S&P 500 simply doesn't hand this rule one. That makes the SPY null a **true negative**.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** STC long/flat net Sharpe **0.29**, HAC *t* = **1.87** (< 2), block-
  permutation **p = 0.96**. Indistinguishable from a shuffled position.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net Sharpe **0.29** vs buy-and-hold **0.65** (Δ −0.36); CAGR
  **2.95%** vs **10.90%** for no extra safety. The long/short version loses money. It destroys
  value versus doing nothing.
- **"Faster MACD"? — BUSTED.** STC (0.29) underperforms the plain MACD (0.42) on SPY and on
  5 of 6 panel names. The defining selling point is false.
